Only allow AI endpoints on this device or your private network (localhost, LAN, Tailscale). Turn off to permit cloud providers — transcripts will leave the device.

Recap records and transcribes your meetings on this device.

WHAT IS STORED
Meeting audio is transcribed to text; the app saves the transcript, your notes, summaries, attendee names, speaker tags, action items, and any photos you attach. All of this is stored in the app's private storage on your device. No account is required.

WHAT LEAVES YOUR DEVICE
By default nothing leaves your device. Two optional features send data out, and only when you turn them on:

• LLM summaries and "Ask this meeting": if you configure an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama, Groq, OpenRouter, or another you choose), the transcript, your notes, and attendee names are sent to that endpoint to generate summaries and answers. Data handling is then governed by whoever operates that endpoint. If you run Ollama on your own computer, the data stays on your own network.

• Cloud speech recognition: the default system transcription engine may use your device's speech-recognition service, which on many phones is Google's and may process audio in the cloud. To keep audio fully on-device, enable on-device Whisper (or your phone's offline recognizer).

TRANSCRIPTION ENGINES
On-device Whisper runs entirely on your phone; no audio leaves the device. The system engine depends on your device's speech service.

CALENDAR
If you enable calendar pre-fill, the app reads events and attendees read-only to fill in a meeting's title and guest list. It never writes to your calendar and does not upload calendar data.

SECURITY
AI can run fully on this phone: the on-device engine loads a local model and never touches the network. When using an endpoint instead, Local-only AI is on by default: the app refuses AI endpoints outside your private network, and plain-http endpoints are never allowed beyond it. Meeting data is excluded from Android's device and cloud backups; use the in-app export instead, which can encrypt the backup with a passphrase (AES-256). You can also require your fingerprint, face, or device PIN to open the app, and block screenshots and the recent-apps preview.

SHARING AND EXPORT
When you share or export a meeting, you choose where it goes; the app does not send it anywhere on its own.

DELETION
Deleting a meeting removes its data and photos from the device. Uninstalling the app removes everything.

CONSENT
Recording people can require their consent depending on where you are. You are responsible for recording lawfully.

This is a starting-point policy for a self-hosted, on-device app; adapt it for your distribution.
A private meeting recorder that transcribes, takes notes, and summarizes — on your device.

• Record and transcribe live, even in the background
• Tag speakers, highlight key moments, snap the whiteboard
• Summaries and "ask this meeting" via a local or your own LLM
• Fully offline transcription with on-device Whisper
• Everything stays on your phone unless you choose to share
By default your meetings never leave this device. Optional LLM summaries and cloud speech recognition send data out only when you enable them — see the privacy policy in Settings.

Recording people can require their consent depending on your location and local laws. Make sure everyone is aware they\'re being recorded. You\'re responsible for recording lawfully.\n\nYour recordings stay on this device unless you share or enable an LLM endpoint.

Silences the speech recognizer\'s repeating start/stop chime by muting media, notification, and system sounds during recording (restored when you pause or finish). Turn this off if you need to hear audio from the phone while recording, e.g. a call on speaker.

Sends the transcript to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint you control — e.g. Ollama on your computer (http://YOUR_PC_IP:11434/v1), Groq, or OpenRouter. When off, a fully offline on-device summarizer is used.
